report.clinical_summary: Patient with HIV (diagnosed ~5 years ago) experiencing new headaches, fatigue, and dizziness for several months. Normal blood work and MRI. On HIV medication (Triumeq) but experiencing side effects (headaches, exhaustion) and not seeing relief for current symptoms. Adherence has been inconsistent ('drug holidays') with headaches returning when doses are missed. Patient feels things are 'slipping out of control' and describes a 'balancing act' between taking responsibility for health and accepting limitations. Expresses frustration about not understanding what's causing symptoms and wants more concrete answers.

evidence.quote: I've been having a lot of headaches and some fatigue that just won't go away. It's really getting in the way of my daily life — work is more stressful than usual, and even spending time with family feels like a chore most days.
When I say 'normal,' I mean feeling like I'm not constantly battling these headaches and fatigue.
It's the difference between feeling like I can actually tackle my day without feeling exhausted by lunchtime or getting easily winded after going up a flight of stairs.
When things are good, it feels like my life is under control again — like I can be present for my family and work without feeling like I'm just going through the motions.

consequences.reasoning: Patient describes substantial impact on daily life - work is more stressful, family time feels like a chore, they're battling headaches and fatigue, get exhausted by lunchtime, get winded easily, and feel like they're 'going through the motions' rather than being present. This is significant interference with their ability to function and be present in their roles.

evidence.quote: These headaches and fatigue have been going on for a few months now, though the intensity has varied.
I was diagnosed with HIV about five years ago, I think.
At first, the medication made things pretty manageable, but lately it feels like everything is slipping out of my control again.

Sometimes it feels like a weight I can't shake off, especially when I miss doses or feel those headaches creeping back up. But at other times, it's more of an abstract thing — something I know exists but isn't dominating my thoughts or feelings.

I can take my medication as prescribed and try to manage my stress levels, but ultimately, I don't know what's causing them or how to fix them.
